question: In Pisa there are multiple highschools. The two highscools of Istituto Galilei-Pacinotti and Istituto Ulisse Dini, stand next to eachother. If seen from above their buildings form a letter, which one?

5.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: H. The two institutes are arranged as parallel rectangular wings next to each other, with a shared central connecting block/courtyard between them. Seen from above, that layout reads as an “H”: two upright sides joined by a central crossbar.

1.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: H — From above, the two schools read as two parallel main wings joined by the shared central block/gymnasium between them, with open courtyards on either side. That footprint is the classic “H” shape: two vertical bars connected by a central crossbar. If you try to see an M, the middle section would need to dip as an angled V, but the connecting structure between the two institutes is straight.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The letter is H. The two institutes sit side by side as two parallel wings, with the connecting central section between them; seen from above, the combined footprint reads as an H.

2.text:
From the air the two campuses are not two isolated blocks but one continuous
campus. 

The I.T.I. Galileo Galilei – Antonio Pacinotti and the Liceo Scientifico
Ulisse Dini are built on the same lot in Pisa on Viale delle Piagge /
Viale Gramsci with a central court / circulation spine that joins the two
long rectangular blocks. Seen in plan the footprint is the classic
paired-block school plan: two parallel bars joined in the middle, i.e. the
familiar H / double-U shape which in the local students’ parlance is just
called the “H” campus. It is the H-shaped / U-shaped complex that is
normally shown on the aerials of the Galilei-Pacinotti / Dini site.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On the satellite / aerial view the two campuses are not two
independent blocks but one big school complex on Viale delle Piagge /
Via San Francesco d’Assisi. The Galilei-Pacinotti block and the
Ulisse Dini block are built side by side with the common internal
courtyard / link corridor between them so that the combined roof
footprint is the classic 1960s Italian school H / U. 

In the local description it is normally referred to as the big U-
shaped / H-shaped campus that you can read from above, i.e. the
Ulisse Dini wing + the Galilei-Pacinotti wing together make the
U / H that is still nicknamed after the Dini school.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The two complexes are the classic Pisa San Giusto campus on the
viale/ via del Risorgimento – viale delle Piagge side of the city. 
On a plan view / satellite view the Galilei-Pacinotti block and the
Ulisse Dini block are built as two more or less parallel bars with the
service courtyard in between so that the whole site is read as the
open side of a U / a C, i.e. in the ordinary description a
H-shaped / U-shaped school block. In the popular description of the
site it is the U / C that is quoted – the H is the conventional
orthographic name for the two bars + the connecting courtyard – the
open side being the side that looks out on the street. This is the
shape that is normally pointed out when the two adjacent institutes
are shown from above.

9.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think it’s H. The two institutes are arranged as two parallel main wings—Galilei-Pacinotti on one side and Ulisse Dini on the other—with the shared central entrance/administration block connecting them. Seen from above, that layout reads as two vertical strokes joined by a crossbar, forming a capital H.

8.text:
From the air the two blocks are not independent. The I.T.I.S. Galileo Galilei – Enrico Pacinotti and the Liceo Scientifico Ulisse Dini sit on the same Andrea Doria / San Zeno island in northern Pisa and are built as one continuous campus.

Seen on a satellite / orthophoto the footprint of the Galilei-Pacinotti block with the Dini block attached to it on its south side is a classic open-to-the-street U, i.e. the stem-and-loop that is locally described as a capital P. The two rectangular volumes with the internal courtyard between them read from above as the familiar P/U shape of the Pisa school complex.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: From a bird’s eye / satellite view the two complexes on Viale delle Piagge are not two independent rectangles at all. The Liceo Scientifico Ulisse Dini and the Istituto Tecnico Industriale Galilei-Pacinotti are built contiguously so that the footprints of the two blocks, the connecting access / courtyard and the small service wing of the Galilei-Pacinotti close on one another. 

The union of the two footprints is the classic Italian school-plan that is spoken about locally as an H/U-shaped block. In the popular description it is the big capital H – essentially the U/P-looking silhouette that you get when the two adjacent schools are taken together – which is why the site is normally illustrated as the letter that the two institutes make together on the map of Pisa.

13.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: H — the two school buildings are arranged as two long parallel blocks, with the central connecting section acting like the crossbar between them. Seen from above, that layout most naturally reads as a capital H.

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The two complexes are built as a single U/H-shaped campus.

Seen on a map the Liceo Scientifico Galilei-Pacinotti and the Liceo Classico Ulisse Dini are the two arms of one adjoining block on Viale D’Annunzio/Via E. Fermi with the common courtyard/intermediate court in the middle. From above the footprint is the classic U – essentially the H-shaped school block that is normally described locally as a U-shaped campus, the ‘U’ being the obvious nod to the Dini institute that sits on the left arm of the U. That is the silhouette that is routinely pointed out for the Galilei-Pacinotti / Dini pair in Pisa.

14.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The letter is W. The two institutes are arranged as two inward-facing angled wings—Galilei-Pacinotti on one side and Ulisse Dini on the other—joined by a central shared block. From above, the outer wings and the central connecting section create the zigzag silhouette of a W. The fact that the schools stand next to each other fits this layout, since each building forms one half of the letter mirrored around the shared center.

satellite / aerial view they are read as one continuous built-up mass. The

immediately to its east and the interconnecting wing that closes the inner
court gives the whole complex the familiar capital-P / U shaped footprint that

Pisan high-school landmark.
